model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; earnings to common after capital retained for balance-sheet growth at the CET1 target, net debt zero; equivalent to residual income on tangible book)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (the CSV Revenue basis: FY2025 5,853 + 2,394 = 8,247). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026; FY0 = 9M-26 actual 6,773 (Q1 2,168, Q2 2,283, Q3 2,322 = NII 1,675 + noninterest income 647, 10-Q Q3-2026 income statement) + Q4E 2,400 (mid-point of the Q4 guide of 2,390-2,410: NII +2.5-3% QoQ, fees +4-5% QoQ). Year 1 = FY2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: 419.20m common shares outstanding at 23 Oct 2026 (10-Q Q3-2026 cover; 421.22m at 30 Sep) plus ~4.5m dilutive RSU/PSU awards (Q3-26 diluted weighted 425.66m vs basic weighted 421.15m). Held FLAT: SBC is charged in the flows, and buybacks ($1,050m FY24, $600m FY25, $650m 9M-26) are how the FCFE is returned, not a separate source of value.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt held at ZERO by construction. Deposits ($185.2bn at 30 Sep 2026) and borrowings (long-term borrowed funds $17,013m + short-term $819m) are operating funding whose cost is inside net interest income; cash and due from banks ($1,041m) is held against that funding. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to common equity at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE ~= net income to common ~2,260 (9M-26 actual 1,637 + Q4E ~620 on the Q4 revenue/expense guide) less capital retained ~640 (4% balance-sheet growth on ~16bn of capital supporting the CET1 target) to hold CET1 in the 10.0-10.5% band (10.5% at Sep-26). Cross-check: 9M-26 NI to common 1,637 less common dividends declared 593 and buybacks 650 = 394 retained while RWA grew $5.8bn (+3.4% in nine months) and CET1 moved 10.6% -> 10.5% -- distributions run slightly ahead of organic FCFE, as at the prior valuation.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory OCF (FY2025 2,211, FY2024 2,001, FY2020 111) is dominated by loans-held-for-sale and trading movements and is not free cash flow for a bank; reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-Q Q3-2026 cash flow statement: share-based compensation $110m 9M-26 (9M-25 $97m); FY2025 $120m, FY2024 $97m, FY2023 $87m (SEC XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense). FY2026E ~$145m, 1.6% of revenue; forward path held at 1.5%. Net-share-settlement withholding was $6-26m a year to 2024 and is not tagged after mid-2024; immaterial and not added.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income is the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026E ~$0.8bn: $300m Q1, $225m Q2, $125m Q3 (10-Q Q3-2026) and ~$150m assumed for Q4. The pace has slowed each quarter as loan growth consumed capital. In October 2026 the Board raised repurchase capacity to $1.95bn (+$1.3bn over the $650m remaining) and the quarterly dividend to $0.52 (+13%, ~$875m a year). An authorisation is capacity, not spend: it does not change FCFE, which is set by earnings less the capital retained for growth. Treated as distribution of FCFE, not modelled separately.
inputs.preferred_note: Preferred stock $2,210m at 30 Sep 2026 (was $2,111m): $400m 6.750% Series J issued July 2026, $300m 4.000% Series G redeemed 6 Oct 2026 (already out of equity at 30 Sep). Ongoing preferred dividends rise from ~$132m to ~$147m a year; Q3-26 charge to common was $37m including a $4m redemption charge. Charged in the flows via the cash_tax_rate_path (see tax note), so value is to COMMON equity and no preferred deduction is made in the bridge.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T21:00:03Z NYSE regular close (Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime)
inputs.book_value_anchor: 30 Sep 2026 (10-Q Q3-2026 Table 22): total stockholders' equity 25,162 less preferred 2,210 = common equity 22,952; less goodwill 8,220 and other intangibles 100, plus related DTL 438 = tangible common equity 15,070 = $35.78 per period-end share (421.22m), down from $38.07 at Dec-25 and $38.29 at Jun-26. The fall is AOCI: -3,682 at Sep-26 vs -2,261 at Jun-26 and -1,970 at Dec-25, i.e. ~$1.4bn of rate-driven securities/swap marks in Q3 as the 10-year Treasury moved from the mid-4s to above 5%. Ex-AOCI tangible book is ~$44.5/share. CFG is a Category IV bank that excludes AOCI from CET1 (CET1 capital 18,673, ratio 10.5%), so the mark does not constrain distributions today and FCFE is unchanged by it; its pull-to-par is an unmodelled upside to book, and its inclusion under a Basel endgame rule the corresponding risk. The stock trades at roughly 1.7x stated TBV. ROTCE (company): Q3-26 15.08%, 9M-26 13.73%, Q2-26 13.91%, FY2025 11.2% -- the Q3 figure is flattered by the lower AOCI-depressed denominator (average TCE 15,759).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: US 10-year Treasury 5.07% (Yahoo ^TNX, 18 Nov 2026 close; weekly closes ranged 4.72-5.28% since mid-August) + beta ~1.15 (regional bank, rate- and credit-cycle levered) x 5.0% US ERP = 10.8%. CHANGED from 10.0% on this update: the 26 Sep build used the same beta and ERP but a ~4.2% risk-free rate, which was below the 10-year at that date (~5.2%); the build is unchanged, the input is corrected. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle and NIM risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branches) are inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin; immaterial relative to $24bn common equity. No lease line, no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; net income equals income attributable to CFG.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity through the component engine, as NAB.AX and IAG.AX; unchanged from the first valuation (2026-09-26). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention is the clean-surplus equivalent and runs through the validated slider engine. UPDATE 2026-11-19 for Q3-2026 (10-Q filed late Oct 2026). CHANGED: (1) anchors -- price, FY0 revenue 9,150 -> 9,173 (Q3 actual 2,322 vs 2,330 assumed; Q4 guide 2,390-2,410 vs 2,370 assumed), diluted shares 424.0 -> 423.7m, balance sheet to 30 Sep; (2) base year-1 pre-tax+SBC margin 35.5% -> 36.0% -- Q3-26 ran 35.8% ((804 + 28)/2,322) and the Q4 guide (revenue +3.4% QoQ, expenses +1%) implies ~36% exiting FY26 even with provision back at ~$140m; years 2-10 were already 36.0% and stay there; (3) cost of equity 10.0% -> 10.8% in all scenarios, a corrected risk-free input (see wacc_rationale) and by far the largest effect. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: growth paths (FY27 +7% needs ~2,454/quarter against a 2,400 Q4 exit rate; NIM 3.18% Q3 and the 3.30-3.50% end-FY27 guide were maintained -- a guide cut or a NIM stall below 3.25% by Q2-27 would move year 1); base margins beyond year 1 and all bull/bear margins (Q3 provision 125 was below net charge-offs 137 with allowance coverage down to 1.29%, so the quarter over-earns on credit; a provision persistently at or below NCOs with NCOs < 35bp would lift base, NCOs back above 50bp would cut it); capital retention paths (RWA +$5.8bn in nine months is consistent with ~4% growth; NOT cut for the AOCI-driven fall in tangible equity because AOCI is outside CET1); cash_tax_rate_path (two offsetting facts: preferred dividends up ~$15m a year adds ~0.4pp, while the effective tax rate ran 21.2% for 9M-26 and 21.3% for FY2025 against 23% assumed -- net cushion ~1.4pp left in place); SBC 1.5%; terminal growth; scenario weights; 15% hurdle. The raised Reimagine target ($225m exiting 2027, >=$450m exiting 2028) is management's own incremental-to-target claim and is in the bull case only, as before. Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income PLUS SBC as % of revenue (FY2025 29.7%; 9M-26 (2,209 + 110)/6,773 = 34.2%; FY2026E ~34.9%); sbc_pct_path 1.5%; da_pct = 0 (D&A is a real bank cost inside noninterest expense); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to grow with the balance sheet, holding CET1 at target; cash_tax_rate_path = income tax PLUS preferred dividends as a share of pre-tax income, so the flow is earnings to COMMON; wacc = cost of equity; net_debt = 0. Residual-income cross-check, P/TBV = (ROTCE - g)/(CoE - g) = (15.6 - 3.0)/(10.8 - 3.0) = 1.62x: on stated TBV $35.78 = ~$58; on ex-AOCI TBV ~$44.5 = ~$72; the engine base sits between because FCFE is driven by regulatory capital, which ignores the AOCI mark. Price is the regular close, not volatile. Metrics.csv has no Q3-2026 core row yet (KPIs only); Q3 statement figures here are read directly from CFG_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR 11.9% diverges >30% from equity 5yr 3.0%: FY2020 EPS ($2.22) is a COVID reserve-build trough, so the 5yr EPS rate flatters. 3yr rates (FY2022 -> FY2025: revenue +0.9%, EPS -1.8%) capture the 2023-24 deposit-cost squeeze. Equity growth is held down by buybacks ($4.4bn FY2021-H1-26) and AOCI swings, not weak earnings.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are not meaningful for a bank (OCF is loan/trading flow); fcf fields left null. FY2022 revenue step-up is the HSBC branch and Investors Bancorp acquisitions (shares 427m -> 495m). FY2026 is tracking ~+11% revenue (9M-26 6,773 vs 6,090) on NIM recovery. CAGRs are FY2025-based and unchanged on the Q3-26 update.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +7%: NIM guided 3.30-3.50% vs 3.22-3.27% FY26 (~+3-4% NII from margin, mid-point discounted) plus ~4% earning-asset growth and fee growth from Private Bank/wealth/capital markets offset by CRE runoff. Tapers to 3% terminal (US nominal GDP ~4% less a mature bank's share loss).
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin + SBC. FY26E ~34.9% (9M-26 34.2%, Q3-26 35.8%, Q4 guide ~36%); year 1 set at 36.0% (was 35.5%) because the exit rate is already there. Reimagine the Bank (target raised to $225m exiting 2027, >=$450m exiting 2028) largely reinvested; provisions normalise from ~0.37% of loans toward ~0.45% through-cycle, which is why the margin does not expand beyond 36%. Steady 34.5% pre-tax margin = ~15.5% ROTCE on ex-AOCI-swing equity, below management's 16-18% end-FY27 target: CFG has historically lagged its return targets.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained = balance-sheet growth (4%, 4%, 4%, 3.5% x3, 3% x4) x tangible common equity, as % of revenue; implied payout 74% FY27 rising to ~82%.
base.cash_tax_rate_rationale: ~23% income tax + preferred dividends as a share of pre-tax income. Unchanged on the Q3-26 update: preferred dividends now ~$147m (was $132m, +~0.4pp) is more than covered by the effective tax rate running 21.2% (9M-26) against 23% assumed.
base.narrative: NIM guidance is met near the low end, Private Bank and fees grow high-single-digit, credit normalises gently, and ROTCE settles ~15.5%.

bull.ebitda_margin_rationale: Top of NIM guide (3.50% FY27), Reimagine benefits drop through, provisions stay ~0.35-0.40% of loans; ROTCE 16% FY27 rising to ~18.6% -- management's 16-18% target delivered and sustained.
bull.capex_rationale: Faster balance-sheet growth (5%, 5%, 4.5%, 4.5%, 4%, 4%, 3.5%, 3.5%, 3%, 3%) retains more capital.
bull.narrative: The Private Bank scales to 15-16 offices at ~25% ROE, record capital-markets and wealth fees persist, NIM reaches 3.5%, and AI productivity lifts ROTCE into the 16-18% target band and holds it -- closing the return gap to higher-quality regional peers.

bear.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY27-28 US slowdown: provisions rise to ~0.8-0.9% of loans (C&I and office CRE), faster Fed cuts compress asset-sensitive NIM toward 3.1%, fees (capital markets, mortgage) cyclical. Recovers only to ~29.5% pre-tax, ROTCE ~12.4% -- the pre-2026 CFG.
bear.capex_rationale: Balance-sheet growth 2%, 1.5% in the downturn, then 3%/2.5%.
bear.narrative: The Fed cuts faster than the NIM guide assumes and a credit cycle arrives in 2027: office CRE and C&I charge-offs rise, capital-markets fees fall, CET1 at the top of a band it has been drifting down through halts buybacks, and CFG reverts to its long-run 11-12% ROTCE.

scenario_narratives.base: Citizens delivers most of its NIM recovery (3.18% Q3-26 to ~3.35% FY27) as swap and securities repricing roll through and deposit betas hold. Private Bank, wealth and capital-markets fees grow high-single-digit while CRE runs off. Reimagine the Bank savings are largely reinvested; credit costs drift up modestly to through-cycle from a Q3-26 provision that sat below charge-offs. ROTCE settles around 15.5% -- where Q3-26 already printed (15.1%) with help from a benign provision and an AOCI-depressed equity base -- short of the 16-18% target, consistent with the company's record of trailing its return goals. With the 10-year Treasury above 5% the cost of equity is 10.8%, and at that rate the market price is close to base value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management hits the top of its FY27 NIM range (3.50%), the Private Bank reaches 15-16 offices at ~25% ROE and drives outsized low-cost deposit growth, AI productivity ($450m by 2028) drops largely to the bottom line, and credit stays benign (NCOs in the 30s bp, strong DFAST results supporting buybacks). ROTCE reaches ~18.6% and holds, re-rating CFG toward higher-return peers.
scenario_narratives.bear: A faster Fed easing cycle compresses the asset-sensitive margin just as a 2027 slowdown lifts C&I and office CRE losses; capital-markets and mortgage fees fall; CET1 at 10.5% with RWA growing ahead of retained earnings forces a buyback pause despite the $1.95bn authorisation. Revenue stalls for two years, provisions roughly double, and ROTCE reverts to ~12% -- the pre-2026 run rate -- so tangible book compounds slowly and the multiple compresses toward ~1.3x TBV.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: a ~15x levered balance sheet with residual office CRE, an asset-sensitive NIM tied to the Fed path, and CET1 at the low end of its band make a credit/rate cycle a genuine tail (the 2023 regional-bank run is recent). Bull cut to 25% because it needs management to hit a ROTCE target it has historically missed AND credit to stay benign. Base 50%. Unchanged on the Q3-26 update: one good credit quarter (NCOs 37bp, provision below charge-offs) is not evidence that the cycle risk has gone, and the $1.4bn AOCI mark is a reminder of the rate tail.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank's free cash flow to shareholders is the earnings it can distribute after retaining enough capital to grow its balance sheet at its CET1 target. Value = PV at a 10.8% cost of equity of earnings to common (after preferred dividends) less that retention; deposits and borrowings are operating funding and are never deducted. The value driver is sustainable ROTCE versus cost of equity: at ~15.5% base ROTCE, 3% growth and a 10.8% cost of equity, fair value is ~1.6x tangible book ex the AOCI swing.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: 10.8% single rate built on a 5.07% 10-year Treasury; each 1pp moves value roughly 12-15% (the 0.8pp correction on this update cost ~$7/share)
ROTCE path: each 1pp of sustained ROTCE is worth ~$4-5/share
Fed path and deposit betas driving the end-FY27 NIM guide (3.30-3.50%; Q3-26 3.18%)
Credit cycle: office CRE and C&I charge-offs (NCOs 37bp Q3-26, provision below charge-offs, allowance coverage 1.29%)
CET1 at 10.5% vs 10.0-10.5% target with RWA growing ~4.5% annualised limits how much of the $1.95bn authorisation can be used
Basel III endgame AOCI inclusion for Category IV banks would pull the -$3.7bn AOCI into CET1 and constrain distributions
